why: One person can attend all meetings exactly when no two intervals overlap. After sorting by start, only neighbours in that order can clash, so it is a single interval-overlap check.
hints: If you sort the meetings by start time, which pairs do you actually need to compare?
In start order, a clash exists if and only if some meeting starts before the previous one ends.
Sort by start, then scan adjacent pairs checking start[i] < end[i-1]. O(n log n) time, O(1) extra.
pitfalls: End times are exclusive: [1,4] and [4,7] do not clash, so use strict <.
A single meeting is always attendable.
Sort first; the input order is arbitrary.
